q2_gaps: degree-modified comparative ("much more", "far more", "slightly more") — Degree attaches to an entity and entails the positive, which a comparative must not, and MoreBy requires a magnitude + unit, so "much" has nowhere to go and is silently dropped
elliptical comparative pro-form "more so" (adjective-phrase ellipsis with an unstated "than"-standard) — the instruction set covers adverbial-comparative ellipsis and VP-ellipsis only

plain indicative conditional: the shape is licensed (Implication) but no truth value is specified for it — the nearest analogues give both (STV 0.9 0.9) (comparative correlative) and (STV 1.0 0.99) (disjunctive-condition split)
notes: Correctly asserts neither clause — the antecedent generic stays a premise and the comparative does not entail the positive — and a ground (variable-free) Implication has precedent in the Xor rules. The ellipsis is resolved the right way ("more so" = more dangerous, standard = planes) with the More argument order (car, plane) correct.
